title: Style Control
summary: Style and Tone = product identity in every AI response

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction to the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? How to make AI speak in your voice — not in the voice of general ChatGPT.
- Why now? Users feel the product through the assistant's tone and text. The same information with a different feeling = a different product.
- What after the lesson? You will write a short Voice Profile for an assistant or content.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: Writing a Product Description
sections.contentMarkdown:
- I requested a perfume description — and got: «Discover the magic of the luxurious scent that captivates hearts...»
- This is not your voice — this is a canned marketing voice. Every AI product without a Style Guide produces the same phrases.
- Personalization = defining the tone and words that represent you — before the user sees the first response.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: AI in Your Voice = Personalized Experience
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Style = form: Formal or Casual? Bullet points or paragraphs?
- Tone = feeling: Calm, Excited, Reassuring?
- Persona = the complete character: «Speak as if you are a coffee expert addressing a beginner».
- In Builder: Voice Profile in the System Prompt = every response sounds like your product — not from any general conversation.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: General Request vs Tone Request
sections.contentMarkdown:
| General Request | Tone Request |
|---------|-----------|
| «Write a perfume description.» — repeated marketing tone: «luxurious», «magic», «captivates hearts» | «Write a perfume description — calm poet tone, two sentences, without ‘luxurious’ or ‘magic’, for readers.» — «A scent that lingers in the room after you close the book.» |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Two Terms to Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Tone | The feeling conveyed by speech — formal, friendly, excited, calm | Email to a client (formal) ≠ Chat with a friend (friendly) |
| Voice Profile | A short description of your product's speaking style — added in the System Prompt | «Short sentences, simple language, without marketing words — replace ‘luxurious’ with ‘comfortable’.» |

sections.contentMarkdown: Clear tone — not by chance: «Execution before theorizing», «no chaos system» — short sentences, clear stance. This is the result of a Prompt that defined the tone: manifesto, without clichés. The same meaning in a «marketing» tone would have sounded like a different product.

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: You are explaining a new tool to beginners — you want them to feel like you are one of them. What is the best tone?
Complex technical — too many terms
Excited friend — simple and friendly
Warning — fear of making a mistake
Explanation: The friend tone comforts the beginner — and this is what you establish in the Voice Profile of the assistant.
bullets: Warning — fear of making a mistake

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Create a Voice Profile
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Write a short Voice Profile for an assistant or your product content. 10–15 minutes. Delivery: 1. Tone in 3 words (e.g., friendly, direct, simple)
2. A word to avoid + alternative (e.g., replace ‘you’ with ‘you’)
3. Before/After example: - General AI response (one line) - Same response in your voice (one line) Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Clear Voice Profile | 60% | Tone is defined — not just «professional»; includes a word + alternative |
| Before / After | 40% | The examples are truly different; the second matches the Profile |
